# xcp: An extended cp

`xcp` is a (partial) clone of the Unix `cp` command. It is not intended as a
full replacement, but as a companion utility with some more user-friendly
feedback and some optimisations that make sense under certain tasks (see
below).

[![Crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/xcp.svg?colorA=777777)](https://crates.io/crates/xcp) 
![Github Actions](https://github.com/tarka/xcp/actions/workflows/tests.yml/badge.svg)
[![Packaging status](https://repology.org/badge/tiny-repos/xcp.svg)](https://repology.org/project/xcp/versions)

*Warning*: `xcp` is currently beta-level software and almost certainly contains
bugs and unexpected or inconsistent behaviour. It probably shouldn't be used for
anything critical yet.

Please note that there are some known issues with copying files from virtual
filesystems (e.g. `/proc`, `/sys`). See [this LWN
article](https://lwn.net/Articles/846403/) for an overview of some of the
complexities of dealing with kernel-generated files.  This is a common problem
with file utilities which rely on random access; for example `rsync` has the
same issue.

## Installation

### Cargo

`xcp` can be installed directly from `crates.io` with:
```
cargo install xcp
```

### Arch Linux

[`xcp`](https://aur.archlinux.org/packages/xcp/) is available on the Arch Linux User Repository. If you use an AUR helper, you can execute a command such as this:
```
yay -S xcp
```

### NetBSD
[`xcp`](https://pkgsrc.se/sysutils/xcp) is available on NetBSD from the official repositories. To install it, simply run:
```
pkgin install xcp
```

## Features and Anti-Features

### Features

* Displays a progress-bar, both for directory and single file copies. This can
  be disabled with `--no-progress`.
* On Linux it uses `copy_file_range` call to copy files. This is the most
  efficient method of file-copying under Linux; in particular it is
  filesystem-aware, and can massively speed-up copies on network mounts by
  performing the copy operations server-side. However, unlike `copy_file_range`
  sparse files are detected and handled appropriately.
* Support for modern filesystem features such as [reflinks](https://btrfs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/Reflink.html).
* Optimised for 'modern' systems (i.e. multiple cores, copious RAM, and
  solid-state disks, especially ones connected into the main system bus,
  e.g. NVMe).
* Optional aggressive parallelism for systems with parallel IO. Quick
  experiments on a modern laptop suggest there may be benefits to parallel
  copies on NVMe disks. This is obviously highly system-dependent.
* Switchable 'drivers' to facilitate experimenting with alternative strategies
  for copy optimisation. Currently 2 drivers are available:
  * 'parfile': the previous hard-coded xcp copy method, which parallelises
    tree-walking and per-file copying. This is the default.
  * 'parblock': An experimental driver that parallelises copying at the block
    level. This has the potential for performance improvements in some
    architectures, but increases complexity. Testing is welcome.
* Non-Linux Unix-like OSs (OS X, *BSD) are supported via fall-back operation
  (although sparse-files are not yet supported in this case).
* Optionally understands `.gitignore` files to limit the copied directories.
* Optional native file-globbing.

### (Possible) future features

* Conversion of files to sparse where appropriate, as with `cp`'s
  `--sparse=always` flag.
* Aggressive sparseness detection with `lseek`.
* On non-Linux OSs sparse-files are not currenty supported but could be added if
  supported by the OS.

### Differences with `cp`

* Permissions, xattrs and ACLs are copied by default; this can be disabled with
  `--no-perms`.
* Virtual file copies are not supported; for example `/proc` and `/sys` files.
* Character files such as [sockets](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/unix.7.html) and
  [pipes](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man3/mkfifo.3.html) are copied as
  devices (i.e. via [mknod](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/mknod.2.html))
  rather than copying their contents as a stream.
* The `--reflink=never` option may silently perform a reflink operation
  regardless. This is due to the use of
  [copy_file_range](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/copy_file_range.2.html)
  which has no such override and may perform its own optimisations.
* `cp` 'simple' backups are not supported, only numbered.
* Some `cp` options are not available but may be added in the future.

## Performance

Benchmarks are mostly meaningless, but the following are results from a laptop
with an NVMe disk and in single-user mode. The target copy directory is a git
checkout of the Firefox codebase, having been recently gc'd (i.e. a single 4.1GB
pack file). `fstrim -va` and `echo 3 | sudo tee /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches` are
run before each test run to minimise SSD allocation performance interference.

  -L, --dereference

  -w, --workers <WORKERS>
          Number of parallel workers.
          
          Default is 4; if the value is negative or 0 it uses the number of logical CPUs.
          
          [default: 4]

      --block-size <BLOCK_SIZE>
          Block size for operations.

  -n, --no-clobber

      --no-timestamps
          Do not copy the file timestamps

  -o, --ownership

### Local copy

* Single 4.1GB file copy, with the kernel cache dropped each run:
    * `cp`: ~6.2s
    * `xcp`: ~4.2s
* Single 4.1GB file copy, warmed cache (3 runs each):

in the copy occurring server-side rather than transferring across the network. For

import tempfile,pathlib,subprocess,os
EXE='/workspace/executable'
def case(ignore,args=None,extra=None):
 with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='xcp-ignore-') as d:
  p=pathlib.Path(d);s=p/'src';s.mkdir()
  for name in ['a.txt','b.log','.hidden','.git/config','.git/objects/o','sub/a.txt','sub/b.log','sub/deep/a.txt','skip/a.txt','keep/a.txt','sub/.hidden']:
   f=s/name;f.parent.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True);f.write_text(name)
  (s/'.gitignore').write_text(ignore)
  if extra:
   for n,text in extra.items():
    f=s/n;f.parent.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True);f.write_text(text)
  cmd=args or ['-r','--gitignore','src','out']
  r=subprocess.run([EXE]+cmd,cwd=d,capture_output=True,timeout=3)
  print('RULE',repr(ignore),'ARGS',cmd,'RC',r.returncode,'OUT',repr(r.stdout.decode()),'ERR',repr(r.stderr.decode()),'FILES',sorted(str(f.relative_to(p/'out'))+('/' if f.is_dir() else '') for f in (p/'out').rglob('*')))
for rule in ['', '*.log\n','a.txt\n','/a.txt\n','sub/\n','skip\n','**/a.txt\n','*.txt\n!a.txt\n','sub/*\n!sub/a.txt\n','.*\n','*\n','[\n','foo\\\n']:
 case(rule)
case('',extra={'sub/.gitignore':'*.txt\n'})
case('',args=['-r','src','out'])
case('src/\n')
case('*.txt\n',args=['--gitignore','src/a.txt','out'])
case('src\n',extra={'../.gitignore':'src\n'})
PY

"""Regression tests for the independently implemented copy command."""
import os
from pathlib import Path
import re
import stat
import subprocess
import tempfile
import unittest

EXECUTABLE = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / 'executable'


class CopyTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='copy-tests-')
        self.root = Path(self.tmp.name)
        self.addCleanup(self.tmp.cleanup)

    def file(self, name, content=b'contents', mode=0o644):
        path = self.root / name
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        path.write_bytes(content)
        path.chmod(mode)
        return path

    def invoke(self, *args, success=True):
        proc = subprocess.run([str(EXECUTABLE), *args], cwd=self.root,
                              stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
                              timeout=5)
        if success:
            self.assertEqual(proc.returncode, 0, proc.stderr.decode())
        return proc

    def test_help_and_version(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.invoke('--version').stdout, b'xcp 0.24.3\n')
        self.assertIn(b'Usage: executable [OPTIONS] [PATHS]...', self.invoke('-h').stdout)
        self.assertIn(b'--no-timestamps', self.invoke('--help').stdout)

    def test_missing_arguments(self):
        proc = self.invoke(success=False)
        self.assertEqual(proc.returncode, 1)
        self.assertEqual(proc.stderr, b'Error: Invalid arguments: Insufficient arguments\n')
        proc = self.invoke('only-one', success=False)
        self.assertEqual(proc.stderr, b'Error: Invalid source: No source files found.\n')

    def test_invalid_options(self):
        proc = self.invoke('--workers=-1', success=False)
        self.assertEqual(proc.returncode, 2)
        self.assertIn(b'invalid digit found in string', proc.stderr)
        proc = self.invoke('--driver=unknown', success=False)
        self.assertEqual(proc.returncode, 2)
        self.assertIn(b'Unknown driver: unknown', proc.stderr)
        proc = self.invoke('--recursive', '--recursive', success=False)
        self.assertIn(b'cannot be used multiple times', proc.stderr)
        proc = self.invoke('-nf', success=False)
        self.assertIn(b'--force and --noclobber', proc.stderr)

    def test_regular_file(self):
        source = self.file('source', b'abcd\0\xffxyz', 0o641)
        os.utime(source, ns=(1000000000123456789, 1000000000987654321))
        proc = self.invoke('source', 'target')
        self.assertEqual((proc.stdout, proc.stderr), (b'', b''))
        target = self.root / 'target'
        st = target.stat()
        self.assertEqual(st.st_mtime_ns, source.stat().st_mtime_ns)
        self.assertEqual(stat.S_IMODE(st.st_mode), 0o641)
        self.assertEqual(target.read_bytes(), source.read_bytes())
        self.assertNotEqual(target.stat().st_ino, source.stat().st_ino)

    def test_overwrite_preserves_destination_inode(self):
        self.file('source', b'x', 0o600)
        dest = self.file('dest', b'a much longer destination')
        inode = dest.stat().st_ino
        self.invoke('source', 'dest')
        self.assertEqual(dest.read_bytes(), b'x')
        self.assertEqual(dest.stat().st_ino, inode)
        self.assertEqual(stat.S_IMODE(dest.stat().st_mode), 0o600)

    def test_no_clobber_fails_without_changes(self):
        self.file('source', b'new')
        dest = self.file('dest', b'old')
        proc = self.invoke('-n', 'source', 'dest', success=False)
        self.assertEqual(proc.returncode, 1)
        self.assertIn(b'Destination Exists:', proc.stderr)
        self.assertEqual(dest.read_bytes(), b'old')

    def test_validation_happens_before_copying(self):
        self.file('source', b'new')
        (self.root / 'dest').mkdir()
        proc = self.invoke('source', 'missing', 'dest', success=False)
        self.assertEqual(proc.stderr, b'Error: Invalid source: Source does not exist.\n')
        self.assertEqual(list((self.root / 'dest').iterdir()), [])

    def test_same_source_rejected(self):
        self.file('source', b'keep')
        proc = self.invoke('source', 'source', success=False)
        self.assertEqual(proc.returncode, 1)
        self.assertIn(b'Cannot copy a directory into itself', proc.stderr)
        self.assertEqual((self.root / 'source').read_bytes(), b'keep')

    def test_recursive_and_target_directory(self):
        self.file('source/sub/a', b'a')
        self.file('source/b', b'b')
        (self.root / 'source').chmod(0o700)
        self.invoke('-r', 'source', 'out')
        self.assertEqual((self.root / 'out/sub/a').read_bytes(), b'a')
        self.assertEqual((self.root / 'out/b').read_bytes(), b'b')
        self.assertEqual(stat.S_IMODE((self.root / 'out').stat().st_mode), 0o755)
        self.invoke('-r', 'source', 'out')
        self.assertEqual((self.root / 'out/source/sub/a').read_bytes(), b'a')
        self.invoke('-rT', 'source', 'out')

    def test_directory_needs_recursive_flag(self):
        (self.root / 'source').mkdir()
        proc = self.invoke('source', 'out', success=False)
        self.assertIn(b'--recursive not specified', proc.stderr)
        self.assertFalse((self.root / 'out').exists())

    def test_multiple_sources(self):
        self.file('a', b'A')
        self.file('b', b'B')
        proc = self.invoke('a', 'b', 'out', success=False)
        self.assertIn(b'Multiple sources and destination is not a directory', proc.stderr)
        (self.root / 'out').mkdir()
        self.invoke('--target-directory', 'out', 'a', 'b')
        self.assertEqual((self.root / 'out/a').read_bytes(), b'A')
        self.assertEqual((self.root / 'out/b').read_bytes(), b'B')

    def test_explicit_nonexistent_target_directory(self):
        self.file('a', b'A')
        self.invoke('--target-directory', 'out', 'a')
        self.assertTrue((self.root / 'out').is_file())

    def test_missing_file_parent_is_not_created(self):
        self.file('a')
        proc = self.invoke('a', 'newdir/out', success=False)
        self.assertIn(b'No such file or directory (os error 2)', proc.stderr)
        self.assertFalse((self.root / 'newdir').exists())

    def test_directory_parent_is_created(self):
        self.file('a/file')
        self.invoke('-r', 'a', 'newdir/out')
        self.assertTrue((self.root / 'newdir/out/file').is_file())

    def test_permission_switches(self):
        self.file('source', b'new', 0o711)
        dest = self.file('dest', b'old', 0o604)
        self.invoke('--no-perms', 'source', 'dest')
        self.assertEqual(stat.S_IMODE(dest.stat().st_mode), 0o604)
        self.assertEqual(dest.read_bytes(), b'new')

    def test_timestamp_switch(self):
        src = self.file('source')
        os.utime(src, ns=(1000000000000000000, 1000000000000000000))
        self.invoke('--no-timestamps', 'source', 'out')
        self.assertGreater((self.root / 'out').stat().st_mtime_ns, src.stat().st_mtime_ns)

    def test_extended_attributes(self):
        src = self.file('source')
        try:
            os.setxattr(src, 'user.test', b'attribute')
        except OSError:
            self.skipTest('Filesystem does not support user attributes')
        self.invoke('source', 'out')
        self.assertEqual(os.getxattr(self.root / 'out', 'user.test'), b'attribute')
        self.invoke('--no-perms', 'source', 'out2')
        self.assertNotIn('user.test', os.listxattr(self.root / 'out2'))

    def test_symlinks(self):
        self.file('source', b'data')
        os.symlink('source', self.root / 'link')
        self.invoke('link', 'out')
        self.assertEqual(os.readlink(self.root / 'out'), 'source')
        self.invoke('-L', 'link', 'deref')
        self.assertFalse((self.root / 'deref').is_symlink())
        self.assertEqual((self.root / 'deref').read_bytes(), b'data')
        self.file('existing', b'keep')
        self.invoke('link', 'existing')
        self.assertEqual((self.root / 'existing').read_bytes(), b'keep')

    def test_nested_dangling_link(self):
        (self.root / 'source').mkdir()
        os.symlink('missing', self.root / 'source/link')
        self.invoke('-r', 'source', 'out')
        self.assertEqual(os.readlink(self.root / 'out/link'), 'missing')
        proc = self.invoke('source/link', 'copy', success=False)
        self.assertIn(b'Source does not exist', proc.stderr)

    def test_fifo_copy(self):
        os.mkfifo(self.root / 'fifo', 0o600)
        self.invoke('fifo', 'out')
        self.assertTrue(stat.S_ISFIFO((self.root / 'out').stat().st_mode))
        self.assertEqual(stat.S_IMODE((self.root / 'out').stat().st_mode), 0o600)

    def test_numbered_backup(self):
        self.file('source', b'new')
        self.file('dest', b'old')
        self.file('dest.~3~', b'previous')
        self.invoke('--backup=numbered', 'source', 'dest')
        self.assertEqual((self.root / 'dest').read_bytes(), b'new')
        self.assertEqual((self.root / 'dest.~4~').read_bytes(), b'old')
        self.assertEqual((self.root / 'dest.~3~').read_bytes(), b'previous')

    def test_auto_backup(self):
        self.file('source', b'new')
        self.file('dest', b'old')
        self.invoke('--backup=auto', 'source', 'dest')
        self.assertFalse((self.root / 'dest.~1~').exists())
        self.file('dest.~0~', b'previous')
        self.invoke('--backup=auto', 'source', 'dest')
        self.assertTrue((self.root / 'dest.~1~').exists())

    def test_globbing_includes_dotfiles(self):
        for name in ['a.txt', '.hidden.txt', 'b.log']:
            self.file(name, name.encode())
        (self.root / 'out').mkdir()
        self.invoke('-g', '*.txt', 'out')
        self.assertEqual(sorted(p.name for p in (self.root / 'out').iterdir()), ['.hidden.txt', 'a.txt'])
        proc = self.invoke('-g', 'nothing*', 'out', success=False)
        self.assertIn(b'No source files found.', proc.stderr)

    def test_glob_errors(self):
        proc = self.invoke('-g', '[', 'out', success=False)
        self.assertEqual(proc.stderr, b'Error: Pattern syntax error near position 0: invalid range pattern\n')
        proc = self.invoke('-g', '***', 'out', success=False)
        self.assertIn(b'wildcards are either regular', proc.stderr)

    def test_gitignore(self):
        self.file('source/.gitignore', b'*.log\nskip/\n')

        self.file('source/a.log')
        self.file('source/sub/b.txt')
        self.file('source/sub/b.log')
        self.file('source/sub/.gitignore', b'*.txt\n')
        self.file('source/skip/file')

        self.assertTrue((self.root / 'out/a.txt').exists())
        self.assertTrue((self.root / 'out/sub/b.txt').exists())
        self.assertFalse((self.root / 'out/a.log').exists())
        self.assertFalse((self.root / 'out/sub/b.log').exists())
        self.assertFalse((self.root / 'out/skip').exists())

    def test_sparse_files_and_drivers(self):
        src = self.file('source', b'')
        with src.open('wb') as f:
            f.seek(1024*1024)
            f.write(b'SPARSE')
            f.truncate(3*1024*1024)
        for driver in ['parfile', 'parblock']:
            proc = self.invoke('--driver', driver, '--block-size', '64KiB', '--reflink=never', '--fsync', 'source', driver)
            self.assertIn(b'Linux kernel may override', proc.stdout)
            dst = self.root / driver
            self.assertEqual(dst.read_bytes(), src.read_bytes())
            self.assertLess(dst.stat().st_blocks*512, dst.stat().st_size)
